newsitem.title: NORWAY: NORWAY JULY OIL OUTPUT UP AT 3.13 MLN BPD - SURVEY.
newsitem.headline: NORWAY JULY OIL OUTPUT UP AT 3.13 MLN BPD - SURVEY.

text.p: Norwegian oil production rose seven percent in July from June to an average 3.13 million barrels per day (bpd) as many fields returned from maintenance and despite several unplanned shutdowns, a Reuters survey of operators in Norwegian waters showed.
In June, Norway pumped 2.93 million bpd.
The July figure does not include 164,049 bpd of condensate output from the North Sea Sleipner developments.
The North Sea Veslefrikk, Oseberg, Brage and Froey developments returned to normal output levels following scheduled turnarounds in June.
But production was down at Saga Petroleum's Snorre and Vigdis fields after both were closed due to technical difficulties.

Output was halted at the 200,000 bpd Snorre platform on July 20 following a power blackout due to a short circuit. The platform's auxilliary generators later suffered a technical fault and the field was closed for a total of five days.

Vigdis managed just six days of production in July due to a series of problems with the gas compressor system. The field was restarted on August 4 at about 40,000 bpd, but Saga said it expected to reach 70,000 bpd soon.
Statoil's 157,000 bpd Statfjord C platform underwent a one-day unscheduled closure and also shut down the Statfjord East and North satellites, which between them pump about 152,500 bpd.

Norwegian output is expected to slide in August because of a heavy schedule of maintenance. Statfjord B, Gullfaks A and B, Sleipner East and West, Troll West, Snorre and Vigdis are all planned to go into periods of turnaround.
